**Why multi-head attention (observed evidence):**

The paper states single-head attention suffers "reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions," which multi-head attention "counteracts" (arXiv:1706.03762, p.1). Page 4 §3.2.2 explains the mechanism: rather than one attention function on d_model-dimensional Q/K/V, the model "linearly project[s] the queries, keys and values h times with different, learned linear projections" and runs attention "in parallel" (p.4). The observed Figure 1 (p.3) shows "Multi-Head Attention" as a single labeled block in both encoder and decoder stacks, while Figure 2 (p.4) depicts it as "several attention layers running in parallel." The Harvard Annotated Transformer diagram (the-annotated-transformer_14_0.png) matches this, showing Multi-Head Attention blocks feeding Add & Norm in both stacks. Multiple heads let the model attend to different representation subspaces jointly.
